cohort: 251 neonates suspected to have sepsis attending University of Gondar Hospital from September/2015 to May/2016.
finding: The isolation rate of bacterial pathogens in neonatal sepsis was high, with nearly 70% of isolates being multidrug-resistant strains, and low birth weight, low Apgar score, preterm delivery, and cesarean delivery were identified as associated risk factors.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was an independent risk factor for neonatal sepsis (AOR=5.2).
gest_age: Preterm delivery (<37 weeks) was a risk factor for neonatal sepsis
birth_weight: Low birth weight (<1.5kg and 1.5-2.5kg) were risk factors for neonatal sepsis
